briefs.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: high-fidelity product design concept board, landscape, sharp readable UI, not implementation.
Primary request: redesign the attached overloaded Navi assistant popup into an elegant compact conversation surface. Input image 1 is a REFERENCE for the existing blue crystalline cube-in-orb avatar with two thin orbit halos and restrained violet visual identity; it is not a pixel-preserving edit target. Preserve the recognizable avatar, do not turn it into a face or robot. Remove all configuration from the popup: settings stay in AI Echo.
Composition: a beautifully art-directed but practical desktop product board with three clearly separated equally sized popover examples side by side, wide generous margins and soft near-black backdrop. Header 'Navi, without the clutter'. Subheading 'Three interaction states · Design concept'. Each example is a DIFFERENT state, not simultaneous avatars. Labels above the examples '01 Ready', '02 Working', '03 Quick question'.
Visual language: almost-opaque deep charcoal panels, faint violet-gray 1px outlines, 16px radii, near-white readable sans-serif type, lavender primary buttons, muted cyan state accents. Restrained shadow and glow confined to the avatar. No huge gradients, glass glare, nested cards, dashboards or long scrollbars. Crisp high-contrast controls with comfortable touch sizes.
Ready popup: the small original orbiting cube avatar is attached just outside its top corner. Header 'Navi' with an expand icon and close icon. Context line 'RealmForge · Untitled Asset'. One clear conversation chip 'Reading chair' with chevron. Short reply 'I’m here. What would you like to build?' Then generous compose field 'Ask Navi…' and send arrow. Compact bottom row with a microphone icon labeled 'Hold to talk', 'Mic off', and overflow menu. A small footer link 'Open AI Echo'. No agenda list, no growth or placement settings.
Working popup: same components, current conversation 'Reading chair'. Text 'Checking the frame before the next stage.' A compact three-step disclosure showing 'Frame · checking', 'Seat · queued', 'Finish · queued'. An outlined 'Stop task' action remains visible. Composer says 'Ask a side question…'. No invented percent or fake success badge.
Quick-question popup: same components. Text 'Which finish should I use?' Two large quick answers 'Oak' and 'Walnut' plus 'Type a reply'. Composer remains accessible. Footer still has microphone state and Open AI Echo.
Constraints: render supplied text accurately, minimize other text. All examples clean and realistic, aligned controls, no browser tabs or Windows taskbar, no analytics charts, no provider selectors, no configuration cards. Image is a proposed visual design, never label features as already live.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: high-fidelity in-context desktop interaction design mockup, landscape.
Primary request: illustrate a renovated Navi companion assisting in RealmForge without covering the work or turning the popup into a settings panel. Input image 1 is a REFERENCE for the existing blue crystalline cube/orb with two delicate halos and purple OS aesthetic. Preserve that recognizable avatar, not a humanoid or face.
Composition: a complete clean RealmForge app workspace fills most of the image. Small tasteful caption outside window 'Navi in context · Proposed design'. App header 'RealmForge' with document 'Reading chair'. Large central 3D viewport showing a modest chair frame on a dark perspective grid, with one prospective seat piece represented in cyan wireframe; label 'Preview only · Not applied'. Slim left hierarchy 'Chair', 'Frame', 'Seat', 'Finish'. Right properties inspector remains completely unobscured, title 'Seat' and fields 'Position', 'Material', 'Dimensions'. Never render or imply construction already applied.
Navi is positioned in an intentionally empty strip beside the viewport and LEFT of the right properties inspector; its one real avatar is attached to a compact opaque near-black popup about 360px wide and 280px tall. Popup anchored so it does NOT cover the selected chair or property controls. Header 'Navi', context 'RealmForge · Reading chair', close and expand icons. Conversation row 'Chair design' with chevron. Reply 'Here’s the next seat piece. Nothing has been applied yet.' Small 'Review in RealmForge' button, input 'Ask about this piece…' with send arrow. Bottom row 'Hold to talk' and 'Mic off'. Small footer 'Open AI Echo'. No growth, source configuration, placement configuration, full agenda or long conversation history in this popup.
Use clear typography, dark charcoal surfaces, restrained lavender selection accents and cyan only for actual highlighted preview. Maintain readable labels, thin borders, generous whitespace and consistent controls. A delicate attention line from the avatar to the previewed seat can indicate pointing, staying behind text.
Add one small lower-margin annotation outside the app frame 'Yields to your work · Settings stay in AI Echo'. No other annotations. No browser tabs, Windows chrome, giant gradients or fake performance metrics. This is a design proposal, not evidence of a running program.

Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity AI Echo desktop settings renovation concept, one dense working screen, clearly captioned "AI Echo settings · proposed layout · example data".
Primary request: Redesign a genuinely complex configuration workspace, not a simplified profile form. The user approved the compact Navi companion style but said AI Echo has far more settings. Demonstrate real information density with legible forms, policy controls and model catalog, inside a scalable settings shell.
Input images: Image 1 is the CURRENT AI Echo settings screenshot, a reference for existing functionality and app identity, not a pixel-preserving edit target. Image 2 is the APPROVED Navi concept, a style reference only for dark charcoal, restrained violet and cyan. Do not reproduce its three-card layout here.
Composition: one flat desktop UI screenshot filling a wide 16:10 canvas, no laptop/device mockup, no dramatic perspective. Settings header across top: "AI Echo" small then "Settings", search box "Find a setting...", close button. Left navigation about 210px wide, main settings canvas broad, slim right section-outline rail about 170px. Do not put a large avatar/profile hero on this operational page. Use readable modern sans-serif, generous enough line height but compact spacing. Mostly near-opaque charcoal surfaces, hairline borders, violet selected navigation, cyan status accents.
Navigation: retain all existing sections with short group labels. "AI SERVICES": Connection (selected), Generation, Voice (with small New label). "NAVI": Navis, Development, Presence. "SYSTEM": Workspace, Knowledge, Interface, Recovery, Diagnostics. No giant tiles.
Main title: "Connection & smart routing".
Scope strip: "Routing configuration" and "Active Navi: AI Echo". Small clear note "Editing identity does not switch the active Navi."
Local section tabs: "Provider" | "Smart routing" (selected) | "Credentials". Small context line "Manual route is retained while Smart routing is on."
Main panel header "Smart model routing" with enabled switch "Use Smart Model Picker".
Four compact aligned fields in two rows: "Model access" dropdown "Free models only"; "Optimization" dropdown "Balanced"; "Per-request cost cap (USD)" field "0.00"; "Daily selection ceiling (best effort)" field "No local ceiling".
One helper line "Provider billing remains authoritative."
Policy row two separate checks: checked "Allow safe approved fallbacks"; unchecked "Use a free model for ambiguous steering".
Broad model-catalog section "Approved model pool" with small "Example catalog" badge and search "Search model, provider or alias", "All providers" dropdown, "Choose models" button. A restrained table, NOT cartoon cards, with checkbox, "Model / provider", "Capabilities", "Route evidence" columns. Three sample rows explicitly generically named "Configured local model", "Configured remote model", "Unverified route"; local row badge "Local", remote row badge "Policy verified", unverified row amber "Review required", not secretly treating unknown as ready. Short illustrative capability chips "Chat", "Structured", "Planner", keep fit and readable. Section help "Selection and evidence are separate."
Below table a compact status strip "Task readiness" with "Chat", "Free steering", "Structured", "Planner", "Artifact" small labels, and note "Compatibility is not execution success."
Then collapsed full-width rows with chevrons "Advanced limits & pricing" and "Privacy & data policies". Section outline rail "ON THIS PAGE": Mode & costs; Approved pool; Task readiness; Limits & pricing; Privacy. Tiny explanatory note "Advanced controls stay searchable."
Persistent footer spans only main content: "2 unsaved routing changes" at left, "Discard routing edits" secondary and "Save routing" violet primary at right. Small footer caption "Proposed scoped save · not implemented". Do not imply all settings globally save or discard here.
Constraints: professional expert-tool UI, functional density, clear grouping and hierarchy, all text accurate, no invented billing guarantees, no fake success charts, no chat box, no giant portrait, no walls of introductory text, no settings in a Navi bubble. This is an illustrative proposed design with sample catalog state, NOT a live screenshot.
